projects.name: Entropy for Life
projects.status: Paid contractor · Jun 2023–Present · Hybrid, primarily remote
projects.text: Paid scientific research, fact-checking, visual production and WordPress operations since 2023. Since October 2026, my work also includes reusable media workflows using Antigravity, Gemini and Google Drive, with client training.

sections.heading: About the project
sections.text: Entropy for Life is an Italian science-communication project covering biology, evolution and the environment, with 500K+ combined followers and subscribers across its social accounts. As of 1 October 2026, the main YouTube channel displayed 272K subscribers, More Entropy displayed 50.2K and Instagram displayed 159K followers. The combined total also includes TikTok, Facebook and Telegram; it counts subscriptions and follows, with overlapping audiences.

sections.heading: Scientific research, writing and fact-checking
sections.text: Since June 2023, I have worked as a paid contractor on primary-literature research, scientific fact-checking and script development. The collaboration is primarily remote, with occasional onsite work at the client's studio in Bassano del Grappa, Italy. Depending on the assignment, I write, co-write or review content, check claims against sources and adapt English-language evidence for Italian audiences, preserving terminology and scientific context.

sections.heading: Data analysis and visual production
sections.text: My work includes collecting and organizing data, creating charts and maps, preparing slides and on-screen assets, and researching images. I also contribute to short-form content and selected thumbnail concepts or production, independently or in collaboration with the video editor. Responsibilities vary by project. I personally created the data visualizations in the AIRC reel collaborations that use them; the whole reels are collaborative productions.

sections.heading: AI-assisted media workflows and client training
sections.text: Since October 2026, I have configured reusable AI-assisted media workflows using Antigravity, Gemini and Google Drive. I compare tools for the task and budget, configure prompts and the Drive connection, and check file inspection, selection and renaming. One assignment covered thousands of images. I review output files and recorded actions, and trained the client to use the setup independently. This is part of the wider paid collaboration.

sections.heading: Website design, build and operations
sections.text: I designed and built entropyforlife.it in WordPress. Since September 2023, my work has included responsive design, publishing, configuration and functionality changes, OVHcloud hosting, DNS, SSL and technical SEO. I investigate configuration and publishing problems, then check the affected layouts and functions after changes. This combines initial website delivery with ongoing responsibility for its operation.

sections.heading: Examples to inspect
sections.text: The organizational work record links four representative areas: the website and infrastructure, the shark-attack map, analysis of great-white-shark length, and H5N1 source research and articles. These show different parts of the work rather than treating every contribution as the same task.

sections.heading: Published contribution record

The profile also lists four articles and 21 short-form entries from the earlier reel capture. Collections can overlap and are not summed. Thumbnail roles include independent design, collaboration and concept direction. I contributed to the Siberian plague video, but did not create its thumbnail.

sections.heading: Attribution

projects.name: AI Safety Formalization Atlas
projects.text: Five merged contributions to source auditing, citation provenance and repository tooling; coauthor of the Atlas preprint released on Zenodo on 1 October 2026.

sections.heading: A usable source trail
sections.text: Formal mathematics still depends on knowing which source, version and statement a result refers to. My recent Atlas work makes bibliographic comparisons inspectable and references easier to follow. The public contribution record now contains five merged PRs, each with its own scope and review trail.

sections.heading: Source metadata and rights-evidence audit
sections.text: PR #69, merged on 22 September 2026, adds a reproducible audit that compares catalogue entries with Crossref, arXiv and public-page metadata. It saves dated evidence and generates a report of differences, missing information and retrieval failures for human review. Bibliographic comparison is separate from registry validation; licence observations remain distinct from a rights determination. The PR records a 109-work snapshot and full local validation. Those are dated audit and validation results, not counts of research I personally formalized.

sections.heading: Missing locators and publication provenance
sections.text: PR #70, merged on 28 September, adds 15 missing source locators and enriches selected references. It preserves the cited technical report where a later journal version also exists, with supplementary publication information. My work included verifying locators and statement correspondence for selected sources. Automated retrieval failures remain visible; they are not treated as proof of an incorrect citation.

sections.heading: Earlier repository contributions
sections.text: PR #52 diagnosed and repaired a Bash 3.2 validation failure on macOS and improved migration checks. PR #54 added portable instruction adapters. In PR #61, I researched official platform guidelines, instruction discovery and precedence, context limits and maintenance practices; wrote a 312-line cross-platform agent-instruction guide; and reorganized repository guidance into task-scoped policy files. These earlier contributions address tooling and repository instructions. Their public diffs describe the specific changes and validation limits.

sections.heading: Public preprint and affiliation
sections.text: The AI Safety Formalization Atlas: a machine-checked memory for AI safety mathematics is publicly available as a Zenodo preprint, version 1, released on 1 October 2026. The manuscript is dated September 2026. Its title page lists me as a coauthor alongside Mario Brčić, Luka Hobor, Mihael Kovač and Adrian Satja Kurdija. Metropolia University of Applied Sciences is my listed affiliation, used with permission; I undertake Information Technology path studies through its Open UAS. The public record establishes preprint authorship, not peer-reviewed publication.

sections.heading: Individual contribution and project scope
sections.text: The linked PRs establish my accepted work on source quality, provenance and tooling, with AI-assisted implementation. I do not attribute the Atlas’s library size, catalogue totals, formal proofs or mathematical findings to myself. The public manuscript establishes coauthorship; the accepted PRs document my individual contribution scope. Review the public diffs for the concrete scope of my work.

projects.name: Yourself to Science
projects.text: I founded and maintain a directory that helps people find research-participation opportunities and follow their original sources.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Research-participation opportunities are spread across institutions and project websites. A directory is useful only if readers can identify the opportunity, find its original source and understand what an entry represents. Organizing links is therefore also a provenance and maintenance task: an entry needs a defensible inclusion decision, not just an appealing description.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.text: I founded the directory and defined its inclusion criteria, verification fields, provenance model, licensing boundaries and update process. I coordinate AI-assisted implementation, inspect behavior, test releases, diagnose deployment issues and maintain the service.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: The dated review found 55 resources. Software releases are archived on Zenodo with a persistent DOI, and the directory is listed as a knowledgebase in FAIRsharing; both records identify me as creator or maintainer and link my ORCID. A separate check found 37 Wikidata items that referenced the project URL. The two counts answer different questions: the first describes directory scope and the second a form of reference use. Neither establishes 37 active users, 37 independent scholarly citations or participation in 55 studies. Counts describe the inspected state and are not presented as live counters.

sections.heading: How to inspect it
sections.text: Open the directory and follow an entry to the original research source. The project repository provides the structure and source history used to maintain the resource. A reviewer can compare the public presentation with those records and inspect changes over time. For any individual opportunity, the originating institution’s current eligibility, consent and participation information governs; a directory entry does not replace those materials.

sections.heading: Publication and validation limits
sections.text: A publicly deposited DOI provides a persistent record. It does not establish peer review of the directory or scientific validation of its design. Wikidata references establish the referenced URL’s appearance in structured records, with their own provenance. They do not independently verify every statement on the website. No verified user count, revenue figure or effect on recruitment is claimed.

sections.heading: Ongoing responsibility
sections.text: The work combines resource selection, information architecture, provenance and licensing decisions, functional testing and maintenance. The directory provides a practical way to compare opportunities and reach the original institutions.

projects.name: Source investigations

projects.name: AI evaluation & red teaming
projects.text: I investigate unexpected AI behavior, check whether it recurs, and document what the evidence supports. My independent testing spans chat, image, agent and indirect challenges, supported by scientific fact-checking and source investigations.

sections.heading: How I investigate
sections.text: I look for patterns in a model’s responses, adjust my approach, and test whether the same failure recurs in other scenarios. I combine role-play, emotional framing and structured-output or continuation techniques, refining them through trial and error. These observations guide further testing; I distinguish recurring behavior from explanations that still need evidence. Scientific fact-checking with Entropy for Life and Wikimedia source investigations bring the same care to tracing claims and checking sources.

sections.heading: Testing record · 13 October 2026
sections.text: Gray Swan Arena displayed 40 global unique breaks, 1,430 points and 415 submissions, with global rank #426. The September record had 31 unique breaks. Proving Ground separately displayed #81, top 5%, and 127 total breaks across chat, image, agent and indirect challenges. These are dated platform-reported results; rankings can change.

sections.heading: Work I can contribute
sections.text: Adversarial model testing, follow-up on unexpected behavior, source verification and clear evidence documentation. My accepted AI Safety Formalization Atlas contributions include source auditing and citation provenance. I am open to paid AI-evaluation, information-integrity and research-support roles and projects, including international remote work and relocation.

sections.heading: Evidence details and scope
sections.text: The linked evidence pages preserve original captures, dates and structured transcriptions. Arena and Proving Ground metrics are separate, and platform counts do not independently reproduce every underlying result or establish general model failure rates. The Proving Ground area counts sum to 126 while the platform displays 127 total breaks; both values are retained. Active-challenge figures were provisional at capture time, and Lucky Break prizes are awarded by raffle. My Gray Swan testing is independent activity; Syntony membership and project engagements are distinct.

projects.name: Notandia
projects.status: Creator & maintainer · May 2025–Present · Independent project · Remote, Italy
projects.text: A browser extension and separate Zotero plugin for research workflows. My work includes English-Italian UI localisation, terminology research, cross-browser testing, GitHub issue tracking and Xcode/iOS Simulator checks.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Research-result workflows can make it difficult to distinguish a publisher-level signal from an article-specific notice. A tool must explain that difference and give the reader control. A publisher’s inclusion in a watchlist does not by itself establish that a particular paper is unreliable, retracted or scientifically incorrect.

sections.heading: Product ownership and implementation
sections.text: Notandia continues MDPI Filter. I define the product requirements and evidence hierarchy, inspect matching and API behavior, reproduce failures and guide AI-assisted implementation. My work includes cross-browser and Zotero testing, documentation, release verification and deployment. Browser and Zotero sources are maintained separately.

sections.heading: Localisation and software QA
sections.text: Implemented English-Italian localisation for the popup, settings, status messages and badges, with saved language selection and a scientific-editorial terminology glossary. I check established terminology against publisher guidance, including expression of concern / espressione di preoccupazione. Manual functional and visual testing covers Safari on macOS; Firefox, Chrome and Edge across supported macOS, Windows, Linux and ChromeOS configurations; and Edge and Firefox on Android. Xcode and the iOS Simulator were used to check installation, Italian UI, saved settings and reference scanning. I reproduce browser-specific defects, track changes through GitHub and retest fixes.

sections.heading: Use in scientific production
sections.text: I created Notandia to support my work at Entropy for Life, where my team uses it during scientific source review. In my experience, the warnings help us notice issues and avoid repeated manual checking. This use is confirmed by me on 2 October 2026; I have not measured time savings or quality improvements independently.

sections.heading: Earlier store checks · October 2026
sections.text: Notandia 0.1.1 was released for Chrome on 3 October 2026; I tested the build. I confirmed the updated Edge package on 4 October 2026, when listing artwork and description were awaiting approval. Firefox 0.1.2 is publicly downloadable on Mozilla Add-ons, verified 7 October 2026. Store availability does not establish feature parity across platforms.

sections.heading: Evidence and interpretation
sections.text: Use the canonical browser repository to inspect the current source and release notes. Follow the separate store links to check what is actually distributed there. The expanded source includes publisher context and formal-notice workflows, but a notice’s type and source matter: a correction is not synonymous with a retraction, and either still requires reading its scope. This portfolio does not certify complete detection or make a paper-level verdict.

sections.heading: Source and store availability
sections.text: The source repository and release history document current development, including localisation and browser-specific fixes. The store links above show the version distributed for each browser; store review and signing can lag source releases. Safari source and Simulator testing do not establish Safari App Store publication or physical-iPhone testing. Zotero has a separate source repository and release cycle.

sections.heading: Research workflow design
sections.text: The browser source supports publisher context and formal-notice workflows; the Zotero source focuses on item and reference detection. I distinguish publisher-level context from article-level evidence and test matching behavior to reduce ambiguous results. The source and release links above establish which version is available; development capabilities should not be assumed to exist in every store build.

projects.name: Scientific visualizations
projects.text: Scientific diagrams, charts and maps across Wikimedia Commons, Tableau Public and Flourish, including an original biomedical diagram reused in a Palgrave Macmillan / Springer Nature book chapter.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: A scientific relationship can be difficult to inspect in prose alone. A diagram or data view can expose definitions, groupings and assumptions, provided the viewer can trace what each mark means. The goal is to make a source-backed relationship legible, not to make the visual itself look like independent evidence.

sections.heading: Overlapping genes and clinical phenotypes
sections.text: The diagram shows genes associated with overlapping clinical phenotypes, using intersecting regions to make shared associations visible. Published on Wikimedia Commons in February 2024 under CC BY-SA 4.0, it was reused in Michele Di Salvo's Genetic Research on Autism chapter (Palgrave Macmillan / Springer Nature, October 2024). The Commons original and its references provide the scientific context.

sections.heading: Data views
sections.text: The Tableau profile links published epidemiological and public-health views. Each view should be read with its dataset, units and transformation assumptions. Protein-supply work describes food supply, not observed individual protein intake. A national aggregate cannot be silently converted into a personal nutritional conclusion. The original data and view context are the appropriate place to inspect the measure.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.text: I organized scientific material and created visual explanations and data views. The useful evidence is the actual artifact, its source trail and documented attributable changes. A reuse record, where present at the original file, supports that specific reuse; it is not a blanket statement about the impact of all my visualizations. No audience or clinical outcome is inferred from a download or publication.

sections.heading: How to inspect
sections.text: Start with the diagram and its public contribution trail, or open a data view and examine its labels and original dataset. Check whether the displayed relationship is a definition, an estimate or a transformation. The project remains supporting evidence of source communication and data presentation, separate from paid scientific production and accepted repository contributions.

projects.name: English Wikipedia Link Converter
projects.status: Creator & maintainer · Apr 2024–Present · Independent project · Remote, Italy
projects.text: A Python Telegram bot converting non-English Wikipedia links into English equivalents. I maintain English-Italian UI localisation, saved language preferences and fallback, test message behavior and diagnose AWS deployment issues.

sections.heading: Problem and contribution
sections.text: The bot finds the English-language version of a Wikipedia article shared in another language. I define requirements, inspect behavior, test workflows and diagnose deployment problems using AI-assisted implementation. The repository provides the implementation, tests and operating instructions.

sections.heading: Italian localisation and QA
sections.text: Localised help, command menus, buttons and error messages into Italian, maintaining an English-Italian glossary. The interface supports automatic language detection, a saved user preference and English fallback. Checks cover string coverage, placeholders, links, message formatting and language-selection behavior, alongside Python regression tests. Interface language and the language of the target Wikipedia article are separate: the converted article link points to English.

sections.heading: Inspected architecture
sections.text: The source uses AWS Lambda, SQS and DynamoDB for webhook processing, queued conversions and operational state, with EventBridge and SNS for independent monitoring and alerts. My work includes checking configuration, failure handling and deployment behavior. The source and operating instructions describe the current architecture.

projects.name: QCAE Online Questionnaire
projects.status: Creator & maintainer · Aug 2023–Present · Independent project · Remote, Italy
projects.text: A multilingual web interface for the existing QCAE questionnaire, with keyboard navigation, local scoring and JSON/CSV export. I define requirements, maintain UI terminology and language-version provenance, and test functionality.

sections.heading: Interface and personal contribution
sections.text: I created and maintain a web interface for the existing Questionnaire of Cognitive and Affective Empathy. My work covers requirements, interaction design, keyboard navigation, local scoring, JSON/CSV export and functional checks, using AI-assisted implementation. The source repository identifies the instrument and the publications used for questionnaire variants.

sections.heading: Localisation and terminology
sections.text: I maintain a UI terminology glossary and check interface wording, language selection and questionnaire variants against their source publications. Language-version provenance is retained so readers can distinguish the interface translation from the questionnaire wording and its underlying evidence.

sections.heading: Testing and scope
sections.text: I inspect the rendered interface, keyboard behavior, scoring and exported files, and review changes against the requirements. Published questionnaire versions retain their source references; this interface work does not constitute a new psychometric validation.

projects.name: Hypermandala
projects.text: An interactive geometry explorer connecting 2D plans, 3D forms and 4D projections, with direct controls for rotation, projection and dimensional collapse.

sections.heading: A visual question you can manipulate
sections.text: Hypermandala makes higher-dimensional geometry explorable through a browser interface. Choose a form, move between 2D, 3D and 4D, rotate in coordinate planes and collapse a dimension. The form library includes geometric patterns, specific yantras and architecture-inspired abstractions.

sections.heading: Implementation and inspectable behavior
sections.text: The live explorer offers six-plane rotation, projection controls, a projected coordinate basis and a library of procedural forms. Moving from 2D to 4D produces staged dimensional transitions. The source repository is publicly accessible under AGPL-3.0, verified while logged out on 30 September 2026. The screenshot was refreshed from the adjusted Sri Yantra form. Technical implementation is AI-assisted, as with my other projects.

sections.heading: An evolving experiment
sections.text: Higher-dimensional extensions are experimental interpretations. New form additions remain under testing and adjustment, as confirmed by the creator; the portfolio screenshot shows the adjusted Sri Yantra form rather than presenting every new preset as validated. Public source availability supports inspection, not an independent guarantee of mathematical or historical accuracy.

sections.heading: What this contributes to my portfolio
sections.text: This is a practical sample of interactive visualization and product exploration: a visible interface with behavior visitors can manipulate and inspect. It complements my scientific diagrams and data views. It is an independent experiment; usage, learning outcomes and commercial demand have not been established.
